ATTACHMENT 2 JUSTIFICATION & APPROVAL FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION for SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITIONS OVER THE MICROPURCHASE THRESHOLD (See FAR Part 2) UP TO SAT (See FAR 13.106-1) Date: 06/29/2026

1. Nature and/or description of the item/service being procured and its intended use (include the anticipated cost):

This project will address elevated radon levels in Quarters 35 through the installation of a certified radon mitigation system and associated health and safety improvements. Testing identified an average radon concentration of 9.5 pCi/L, which exceeds the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) action level of 4.0 pCi/L. The mitigation system will serve the entire apartment complex, consisting of eight units and approximately 4,389 total square feet..

2. Sole Source Justification rationale (Check one and explain below):

______ Only one responsible source.

_X_: Urgent and compelling circumstances exist. Include critical delivery or performance dates, and when you became aware of the requirement. Provide a specific statement of the impact on Government operations, financial or otherwise, if the required delivery or performance dates are not met. ______ Other _________________________________________________ Explain:

The Park conducted radon testing in March 2026 and identified radon levels in Quarters 35 that exceeded the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) action level of 4.0 pCi/L. A contractor was subsequently engaged to verify the test results. The verification testing confirmed that the average radon levels were approximately twice the EPA action level.

The immediate installation of a certified radon mitigation system is necessary to reduce the elevated radon levels and mitigate the potential health risks to employees residing in Quarters 35. Without immediate corrective action, employees will continue to be exposed to radon levels substantially exceeding the EPA action level. Continued exposure presents a potential long-term health risk and requires prompt mitigation.

The critical path for completing the radon mitigation work is essential. The contractor and funding necessary to immediately address the condition are available. Delaying the procurement to conduct additional market research or to follow a longer acquisition timeline would unnecessarily delay installation of the mitigation system and prolong employee exposure to elevated radon levels.

Last updated 6/2/2016 The impact of delay to Government operations is significant because Quarters 35 is employee housing and continued occupancy would result in ongoing exposure to radon levels approximately twice the EPA action level. Immediate procurement and installation of the radon mitigation system is therefore necessary to promptly address the elevated radon condition and reduce the potential health risks to employees. The urgent and compelling circumstances do not permit the delay associated with a longer acquisition process.

3. Market Research. Please explain the results or why one was not performed. State whether any other offers were received or anyone expressed interest:

Park reached out to local radon mitigation contractors. Upper Edge responded immediately and was on site within a few days. They verified our findings and provided immediate corrective actions.

Due to the urgent and compelling need to mitigate the elevated radon levels and protect the health and safety of building occupants, limited market research was not conducted. Immediate action is necessary to install a radon mitigation system. The time required to conduct additional market research and complete a longer period of acquisition planning and processing would delay the installation and result in continued exposure to elevated radon levels. Such a delay would have a negative impact on the health and safety of building occupants. Therefore, immediate procurement of radon mitigation services is necessary.
